changes.old: MSL port 'msl_0': only 2 substrate cell(s) in z (h_sub=254µm, dx=127µm). Yee staircase at the dielectric interface is O(dx), not O(dx²), for inhomogeneous ε, so Z0 accuracy degrades linearly as the substrate is under-resolved. Refine to dx ≤ 63.5µm (4+ substrate cells) AND keep h_sub/dx an integer (aligned); this check's accuracy target is <5% Z0 bias against the DECLARED-board Hammerstad-Jensen anchor (S is normalized to that anchor, issue #723). No specific measured bias percentage is quoted here (audit 2026-09-02): the 2026-08-02 sweep's aligned rows are a pre-#802 as-solved record — the exact-coordinate rasterizer (#802/#834) moved three of their realized trace widths, and a re-solve of aligned h_sub/3 on the current rasterizer contradicted the retired figure — so re-run scripts/diagnostics/msl_z0_bias_floor_sweep.py before quoting one as a live bound.
changes.new: MSL port 'msl_0': only 2 normal interval(s) between the validated ground and trace planes. Validated conductor-plane gap=254.0µm over 2 normal interval(s), from z=0.0µm to 254.0µm (declared height=254.0µm). Separately, the declared-material column has 2 same-permittivity sample slot(s), extent 254.0µm. This material extent is not the conductor-plane gap. The existing resolution recommendation is at least 4 normal intervals and an aligned declared substrate interface. On a uniform mesh, refine to dx ≤ 63.5µm and align the declared ground z=0.0µm and trace z=254.0µm with nodes; on a profiled mesh, place sufficient nodes between those faces. Geometry screening does not quantify Z0 error. The historical sweep and its realized-board Hammerstad-Jensen anchor are pre-#802 records; a new matched-geometry measurement is needed before quoting a current accuracy bound.
